purpose: Exercise bd 1.3.0's dead-worker recovery path (create issue, claim it in_progress, let the lease go stale, run `bd reclaim`) in a scratch database outside any tracked repo, to test whether catalogs/foundation/decisions.json id=dependency-task-queue's limitation 'A queue is not worker cancellation, distributed lease correctness or restored task-effect acceptance' can move from not_established to an actual pass/fail receipt for crash/recovery semantics.
preregistered: Prediction before running: (1) `bd reclaim --older-than 0s` run immediately after claim will be a no-op (count 0) because the lease has not yet expired; (2) after real elapsed time exceeds the lease TTL, the same `bd reclaim --older-than 0s` invocation will revert the issue's status from in_progress back to open/ready and clear its assignee, and the issue will then be listed as claimable again. bd's own reclaim --help documents this exact stale-lease reaper semantics ('reverts the issue back to ready so another worker can claim it'). Would settle the gap toward supports_incumbent if both hold; toward refutes_incumbent if the lease never gets reclaimed once genuinely stale; inconclusive if the probe cannot establish the lease's real expiry (e.g. TTL not discoverable).

commands.cmd: mkdir -p /tmp/beads-gap-probe && cd /tmp/beads-gap-probe && git init -q . && git config user.email probe@example.com && git config user.name probe && $HOME/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/bin/bd init -q
commands.output_excerpt: Installed Claude/Codex/Cursor hooks and skill scaffolding under the scratch dir only (CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, AGENTS.md, .agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md); created .beads/embeddeddolt/ local storage. No global (~/.claude, ~/.config) files were touched (verified with `find ~/.claude -newer ... -type f` returning empty).

PILOT RUN (superseded, see limitations): status -> in_progress, assignee -> probe-worker, started_at 2026-09-22T22:48:45Z. Response omitted lease_expires_at/heartbeat_at fields present on a bare --claim reply -- CORRECTED interpretation (fix round, see limitations): this is not a sign the lease went to the wrong holder. Per upstream source at the pinned commit, --claim arms a lease for the actor, but the same call's --assignee value is then applied through the ordinary generic-update path, and ManageLeaseOnUpdate (internal/storage/issueops/update.go) treats any assignee change on an in_progress issue as ending/transferring the claim, which deletes the lease row outright (DeleteLeaseInTx). So this issue never had a lease row at all after the combined call returned, not a lease 'granted to the actor instead of the assignee'.

commands.cmd: $BD reclaim --older-than 0s --id beads-gap-probe-3cg --json -v   # PILOT: run immediately after claim
commands.output_excerpt: {"count":0,"reclaimed":null,"scoped":true}  -- correctly a no-op while lease is live, as preregistered

commands.cmd: sleep 330; $BD reclaim --older-than 0s --id beads-gap-probe-3cg --json -v   # PILOT: ~5m59s after claim, i.e. ~59s past the source-confirmed 5-minute DefaultLeaseTTL
commands.output_excerpt: {"count":0,"reclaimed":null,"scoped":true} -- unexpectedly STILL a no-op past the nominal TTL. CORRECTED root cause (fix round, see limitations): reclaim's own query (ReclaimExpiredLeasesInTx, internal/storage/issueops/lease.go) is `SELECT ... FROM leases l JOIN issues i ON i.id = l.issue_id WHERE i.status = 'in_progress' AND l.lease_expires_at < ?` -- an inner join against the leases table. The pilot's `--claim --assignee <other>` call armed a lease for the actor, but its own --assignee field-patch then ran through the generic-update lease manager (ManageLeaseOnUpdate), which deletes the lease row whenever an update changes who holds an in_progress claim. With no leases row left, the JOIN excludes the issue from every future reclaim scan regardless of how stale it gets -- there was no lease to expire, not a lease misdirected to the wrong holder. Full transcript retained at raw_artifacts[0].

commands.output_excerpt: const DefaultLeaseTTL = 5 * time.Minute  -- confirms the pilot's wait window (330s) was genuinely past the real TTL, ruling out 'TTL longer than assumed' and pointing at the --claim+--assignee confound instead.

Follow-up show: status:"open", no assignee field, started_at cleared, updated_at:"2026-09-22T23:05:01Z" (revert landed 55s after the 23:04:06Z expiry). `bd list --status open --json` lists beads-gap-probe-84a again, confirming it is claimable. Full transcript retained at raw_artifacts[1].

result: bd 1.3.0's documented dead-worker recovery path works as specified when invoked the way its own docs describe (`bd update <id> --claim`, then `bd reclaim`): a claimed issue's lease is correctly left untouched by `bd reclaim --older-than 0s` while live, and is correctly reverted to status=open with assignee/started_at cleared, and re-listed under `bd list --status open`, once real elapsed time exceeds the compiled 5-minute DefaultLeaseTTL (observed transition landed 55s after the recorded lease_expires_at). CORRECTED (fix round, see limitations): combining --claim with an explicit --assignee flag on the same `bd update` call (the exact form the triage's own proposed command list used) does NOT grant the lease to the CLI actor identity instead of the stated assignee -- the claim first arms a lease for the actor, then the call's own --assignee field-patch runs through the generic-update lease manager, which deletes the lease row whenever an update changes who holds an in_progress claim. The pilot issue was therefore left in_progress with NO lease row at all, and `bd reclaim`'s query is an inner join against the leases table, so an issue with no lease row can never be selected by reclaim, however long it sits stale -- permanently, not just at the 0s-grace/~59s-past-TTL window this pilot happened to test. This is a real, permanent limit on bd's crash-recovery semantics for any issue whose in_progress claim was established or transferred through a generic update rather than the bare lease-arming `--claim` verb (bd's own source names this pattern bd-9hpgf/GH#4716), not merely a usage trap confined to this one invocation.

verdict_impact.explanation: Moves catalogs/foundation/decisions.json id=dependency-task-queue's 'distributed lease correctness' limitation from wholly not_established to a single successful native execution of bd's stale-lease reclaim path (crash/recovery semantics for ONE claimed issue, ONE local embedded-dolt store, ONE reaper invocation). It does not establish worker cancellation, multi-replica federation semantics (the reclaim --help's replica-guard/--any-replica behavior was read but not exercised), concurrent-reclaim races, or production-scale reliability. CORRECTED (fix round): before narrowing that limitation, the decision text should also record the newly-confirmed permanent gap below -- reclaim only recovers issues claimed via the bare lease-arming `--claim` verb, and never recovers an in_progress issue whose status/assignee was set or transferred through a generic update -- rather than describing 'distributed lease correctness' as uniformly covering any in_progress claim.

limitations: CORRECTED (fix round): dead-worker recovery via `bd reclaim` only covers issues claimed through the bare, lease-arming `--claim` verb (or `bd ready --claim`). `ReclaimExpiredLeasesInTx` (internal/storage/issueops/lease.go, pinned commit f45b249ce6b40ba62aecc03949e6371e8f7c79d8) selects `FROM leases l JOIN issues i ... WHERE i.status = 'in_progress' AND l.lease_expires_at < ?`, an inner join against the leases table, and `ManageLeaseOnUpdate` (internal/storage/issueops/update.go) deletes an issue's lease row (DeleteLeaseInTx) whenever a generic update changes who holds an in_progress claim -- including the combined `--claim --assignee <name>` form this triage's own proposed command list used. Any issue left in_progress (or reassigned while in_progress) through such a generic update therefore has no lease row and is permanently unreachable by `bd reclaim`, at any elapsed time, not just within this probe's 0s-grace/~59s-past-TTL window. This is a real, permanent limit on bd's crash-recovery semantics -- not a usage trap confined to one invocation -- and it should be recorded in catalogs/foundation/decisions.json id=dependency-task-queue's limitations text before that text is narrowed on the strength of this probe's positive (bare --claim) result.
Single trial, single machine, single embedded-dolt store, single issue per run: no statistical confidence on timing precision or on races between a live heartbeat and a concurrent reclaim.

The pilot run (superseded by the corrected run above) combined `--claim` with an explicit `--assignee` flag, which the reclaim result at ~59s past the nominal TTL never picked up. This is retained in the receipt as its own honest, unresolved-until-diagnosed negative result rather than discarded; the corrected root cause (the combined invocation's generic assignee-update deletes the lease row entirely, per the first limitation above) was established by reading gastownhall/beads source at the exact pinned commit, not by further live experimentation on that same issue. An earlier version of this receipt (superseded by this fix round) mischaracterized the mechanism as the lease being granted to the CLI actor identity rather than the stated assignee; the actor does receive the initial lease, but it is then deleted outright by the assignee update, not merely misdirected.

Multi-replica / federation reclaim guard behavior (--any-replica, granted_node scoping, cross-store sync-interval invariants) was read from source and `bd reclaim --help` but not exercised: this probe used a single node with no BEADS_NODE_ID configured.

`bd sql` refuses raw queries against the embedded-dolt backend ('not yet supported in embedded mode'), so the leases table could not be inspected directly; all lease state was inferred from `bd show --json`'s lease_expires_at/heartbeat_at fields and `bd reclaim -v`'s own JSON output.

Does not establish worker cancellation (a live worker being forcibly stopped) or restored task-effect acceptance (whether a reclaimed issue's prior partial work product is safe to resume) -- both explicitly named as separate from this decision's own limitations text and out of scope for this probe.

All state is confined to /tmp/beads-gap-probe (outside any tracked repo) and was not committed; the scratch database and its two synthetic issues are disposable and were not registered with any live ai-memory/Qdrant/Dagu service.
